# [BUG] Movie browsing bypasses dynamic backend resolution; local tunnel URL not auto-discoverable

## Bug
Two compounding issues, both regressions against #146's zero-touch goal, confirmed live:

1. `services/TMDB.js` (the baseQuery behind Movies/Actors/Genres/Search/RatedCards — i.e. the whole app's real content) uses a static `fetchBaseQuery({ baseUrl: VITE_API_URL || 'https://api.themoviedb.org/3' })`. It never reads `filmpire_api_url` (localStorage) or does any health-based routing the way `media.js`/`user.js` already do via `createDynamicBaseQuery`. With `VITE_API_URL` unset in Vercel, it silently talks to the real themoviedb.org instead of our own gateway.
2. The Admin Dashboard's 'Local Tunnel' connect button used a hardcoded `ACTIVE_TUNNEL_URL` constant. cloudflared quick tunnels (`start-tunnel.sh`) mint a brand-new random `*.trycloudflare.com` hostname on every restart, so that constant goes stale the moment the tunnel is restarted, and nothing published the current one anywhere the deployed frontend could discover it automatically.

Net effect: with Azure/AWS down, a fresh visitor to https://filmpire-microservices-tan.vercel.app/ gets no working backend at all unless someone manually visits /admin, clicks Connect, and the hardcoded tunnel constant still happens to be current.

## Root Cause
See above — no shared, always-current source of truth for 'which backend is actually reachable right now', and one service (TMDB.js) was never wired into the dynamic-resolution mechanism the others use.

## Severity vs. Priority
**Severity (technical impact):** Critical
**Priority (business urgency):** P1
